lead: Each blank needs the word that normally goes with its neighbour. Several options may look right in Chinese, but only one is the natural English partner.
每個空格要選的是和旁邊的字「慣用搭配」的那個字。中文看起來幾個選項都通，但自然的英文搭配只有一個。
steps: Find the word right next to the blank: usually a noun after it or a preposition before it.
先找空格緊鄰的字：通常是後面的名詞，或前面的介系詞。
Say the phrase in your head with each option. Choose the one you have heard or read together.
把每個選項放進去默念，選你聽過、讀過會連在一起的那個。
Check the small words around it (into, of, on, to). They are part of the phrase.
檢查周圍的小字（into、of、on、to），它們也是搭配的一部分。
If two options both fit, read the whole sentence for the exact meaning.
如果兩個選項都說得通，就讀全句，看確切語意。

head: Verb + noun: the noun picks the verb
動詞 + 名詞：由名詞決定動詞
body: English does not use one verb for every noun. Learn the pair as one block. Different nouns take different verbs, even when the Chinese verb is the same.
英文不會一個動詞通用所有名詞。把搭配當成一整塊背。中文用同一個動詞，英文名詞不同，動詞就不同。
ex: The committee reached an agreement after a short discussion.
委員會在短暫討論後達成協議。
Ms. Tan conducted a survey of customer habits.
Tan 女士針對顧客習慣做了一項調查。
The agency launched a new advertising campaign.
該機構推出了新的廣告活動。

head: Small words belong to the phrase
小字也是片語的一部分
body: Some phrases need a preposition in a fixed place. Without it, a similar phrase may mean something else or not exist. Check what comes before and after the blank.
有些片語的介系詞位置是固定的。少了它，可能變成別的意思，或根本不存在。要看空格前後。
ex: The new tax rule came into effect in March.
新的稅務規定在三月生效。
Mr. Ito is in charge of the Osaka branch.
Ito 先生負責大阪分公司。
She spoke on behalf of the whole team.
她代表整個團隊發言。

head: Adverb + adjective or verb: not interchangeable
副詞搭配：不能隨意替換
body: Adverbs such as highly, strongly, greatly and heavily all add strength, but each keeps its own partners. Learn the common pairs instead of guessing from the meaning.
highly、strongly、greatly、heavily 都有加強語氣的作用，但各有固定夥伴。要記常見搭配，不要憑字義猜。
ex: This model is highly recommended by our technicians.
我們的技師高度推薦這款機型。
We strongly advise customers to back up their files.
我們強烈建議顧客備份檔案。
The firm depends heavily on a few large clients.
這家公司非常依賴少數幾個大客戶。

head: Same meaning in Chinese, different verb in English
中文同一個詞，英文不同動詞
body: Say “提出” in Chinese and you can mean raise, submit, file or propose. The noun decides which: a concern is raised, a form is submitted, a complaint is filed, a plan is proposed.
中文都說「提出」，英文可能是 raise、submit、file、propose。看名詞：疑慮用 raise，表格用 submit，申訴用 file，計畫用 propose。
ex: Several staff raised concerns about the new schedule.
數位員工對新班表提出疑慮。
Applicants must submit the form by Friday.
申請人必須在星期五前提交表格。

head: Time and manner phrases are fixed too
時間與方式片語也是固定的
body: Phrases about timing keep their own preposition and noun: in advance, on time, ahead of schedule, at short notice. Changing one word often breaks the phrase.
表示時間的片語，介系詞和名詞都是固定的：in advance、on time、ahead of schedule、at short notice。換掉其中一個字，常常就不對了。
ex: The caterer can deliver at short notice if we call before noon.
如果我們中午前打電話，外燴業者可以臨時送餐。
Please book your room well in advance.
請提早預訂您的房間。

head: Look for the verb that fits the whole phrase
要挑適合整個片語的動詞
body: Wrong options are often real verbs that go with other nouns. Ask what the noun normally does: a vacancy is filled, a meeting is held, a goal is set, a profit is made.
錯誤選項常是別的名詞的搭配動詞。想想這個名詞通常怎麼用：職缺用 fill，會議用 hold，目標用 set，利潤用 make。
ex: The hotel is trying to fill two vacancies in housekeeping.
飯店正在設法補齊房務部的兩個職缺。
Management will set new sales targets next month.
管理階層下個月將訂定新的銷售目標。

pairs.right: The two firms reached an agreement on delivery dates.
pairs.wrong: The two firms got an agreement on delivery dates.
why: An agreement is reached, not got.
協議是用 reach 達成的，這裡不用 get。

pairs.right: The contract came into effect on March 1.
pairs.wrong: The contract came effect on March 1.
why: Come needs into before effect. Take effect needs no preposition.
come 後面要有 into；take effect 則不需要介系詞。

pairs.right: Please pay attention to the safety notice.
pairs.wrong: Please pay attention on the safety notice.
why: The fixed phrase is pay attention to.
固定說法是 pay attention to。

pairs.right: The firm depends heavily on a few large clients.
pairs.wrong: The firm depends highly on a few large clients.
why: Depend goes with heavily. Highly goes with words like recommended and competitive.
depend 搭 heavily；highly 多搭 recommended、competitive 這類字。

head: Verb + noun in business
商務常見動詞 + 名詞
Fixed phrases with prepositions
含介系詞的固定片語
Adverb + adjective or verb
副詞 + 形容詞或動詞
More set phrases with verbs
其他動詞慣用語

traps: Do not translate word by word from Chinese. English says make a decision and make a mistake, not do a decision or do a mistake.
不要逐字從中文翻。英文是 make a decision、make a mistake，不是 do a decision、do a mistake。
Options that look like synonyms are usually other words' partners. If an option goes naturally with a different noun, it is probably the trap.
意思相近的選項，通常是別的名詞的搭配。如果某個選項明顯屬於另一個名詞，它多半是陷阱。
A phrase goes wrong when a small word is missing or changed. Come into effect is fine, but come effect is not. Read the words just before and after the blank.
片語少了小字或換了小字就不對。come into effect 可以，come effect 不行。要看空格前後的字。
